scope.comparison: Actual working-tree diff versus local origin/main, restricted to scripts/project_authority.py and tests/test_project_authority.py.
scope.adjacent_code: Read project identity, inventory, approval and status paths; workflow_state control_directory/active_anchor; project_admin CLI; validate_workflow_approval digest, JSON, safe-file and read-only Git helpers.
acceptance: Unknown inputs use SHA-256 of original bytes. Allowlisted text suffixes and Dockerfile normalize line endings only after successful UTF-8 decoding and absence of NUL; invalid UTF-8 or NUL-containing inputs retain raw-byte hashing.
Binary CRLF-to-LF changes in runtime and config invalidate approval; known Python text CRLF-to-LF retains portability. Added tests check inventory and active approval behavior.

Identity parsing is inside the status exception boundary. Missing, malformed and interrupted identity returns AWAITING_APPROVAL with a blocker; status does not invoke registration, locking, state initialization or writes.

applies() now treats the checkout authority operation.lock as evidence of project authority even before identity registration. workflow_state.active_anchor therefore routes to the project gate and refuses missing project inputs instead of inheriting legacy approval.

The new historical-export regression establishes that legacy active_anchor initially succeeds, creates only the authority operation.lock before registration, then requires applies() to be true, active_anchor to raise, and status to return AWAITING_APPROVAL with a blocker while preserving the lock contents. This models the on-disk residue of a hard interruption; it does not simulate process termination.

The final diff adds six parameter-expanded cases plus an interrupted-status assertion without deleting or weakening prior assertions. Missing/malformed status tests cover direct and CLI results and repository/host authority file-byte preservation.

The reviewed two-file diff contains three narrow supporting-gate corrections and regression coverage. It does not widen paid, provider, publication, pilot, merge or deployment authority, change application code, or expand the reusable OOP architecture scope.

verification_limitations: Static acceptance review only. No suites, providers, workers, Docker, source mutations or Git writes were performed. The only intentional file write was this report.
The independently running final 35-case lifecycle suite result was not observed and is not asserted here.
Invalid-UTF-8 and NUL-containing known-text fallback branches were inspected statically; the added regressions do not directly exercise those two branches.
The new pre-registration interruption regression asserts lock preservation, not a complete repository/host byte snapshot. Read-only behavior for that path was checked by source inspection.

Application-wide changes and broader architecture were outside this bounded review. origin/main was inspected as locally available without fetching. All four raw hashes were rechecked against the final observed source bytes before saving; the main agent must validate them before commit.
